source.title: SIGUA: Forgetting May Make Learning with Noisy Labels More Robust
source.authors: Bo Han; Gang Niu; Xingrui Yu; Quanming Yao; Miao Xu; I. Tsang; Masashi Sugiyama

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own test-accuracy trajectory over training epochs and explicitly identifies the corresponding CIFAR-100 test-error pattern as epoch-wise double descent. This is a conceptual test in a noisy-label learning setting, not a reproduction of the original study's full method.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on epoch-wise double descent, but the CIFAR-100 result is its own. Other noisy-label performance comparisons do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study's own CIFAR-100 noisy-label runs (9-layer CNN, 200 epochs) show test accuracy falling then rising again. The authors call this epoch-wise double descent in test error (Appendix B). It is an incidental, qualitative observation in a new setting (a noisy-label learning method) rather than a study designed to test the claim, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the emphasis should be on SIGUA. The main conclusion is that SIGUA (gradient descent on good data, underweighted ascent on bad data) robustifies self-teaching and backward correction, often significantly. The epoch-wise double-descent remark is a side observation on CIFAR-100: accuracy recovered and surpassed the early-stopping best. The introduction uses such phenomena to argue against relying on early stopping.
record.recipe_differences: No model-size or sample-size sweep; the reported temporal pattern comes from noisy-label experiments with test accuracy plotted over epochs.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML); the text identifies the proceedings as PMLR 119, 2020.
record.problems: The epoch-wise double-descent finding is qualitative and restricted to CIFAR-100. Although separate curves are plotted for methods and noise conditions, the prose does not identify which curve or condition supports its description; no numeric trajectory values are given there.
record.rows_left_out: No individual method-by-noise curves were added as separate rows because the text's explicit epoch-wise double-descent statement does not attribute the finding to a particular curve or condition; the figures provide curves without textual attribution or numeric values.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; the ResNet-18 vs 9-layer CNN comparison (Table 8) is a two-point method comparison, not a capacity sweep around interpolation.
Only CIFAR-100 is described as double descent; no numeric trajectory, no attribution to a specific method or noise level, and no check across models or with a constant learning rate.
No non-deep model classes or capacity sweep past interpolation.
Noise levels vary, but the study does not relate peak presence or size to noise, multiple peaks, or tuned regularization.

missing.what: Test-accuracy-over-epochs curves for Standard, Self-Teach and SIGUA_SL on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and NEWS, and for BC/nnBC/SIGUA_BC on all datasets. These show accuracy decreasing after early learning, and the text states no second rise except for CIFAR-100. They bear on how general V2 is in this setting, but values exist only in the figures.

record.verdict_notes: Nakkiran et al. 2020 (an original source) is cited only as motivation. Figure 1 (MNIST, StopGrad/SIGUA) uses a deliberate switch at epoch 150 using true labels, so it does not bear on V2. Comparisons of methods in Tables 1–3 and 8 are the study's own method evaluations, not tests of the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep testing test error around an interpolation threshold.

The reported result is limited to CIFAR-100 in SET1; the text does not identify the particular curve or noise condition underlying the statement, and does not test whether the pattern generalizes across models or settings.
No sweep over training sample size near an interpolation threshold.
No general comparison across model classes or capacity sweep past interpolation.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested against peak locations.
The study varies label-noise conditions but does not test whether noise drives the peak, whether multiple peaks arise, or whether tuned regularization removes it.
No re-counting of model complexity by effective parameters.

rows.subject: 9-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy over training epochs; authors describe the inverse test-error trajectory as epoch-wise double descent.

conditions.value: symmetry-20%, symmetry-50%, and pair-45% are shown in separate figure panels; the text does not attribute its description to a particular panel
SET1 methods are plotted; the text does not identify which method's curve it describes

rows.measure: Test accuracy over epochs; interpreted by the authors as epoch-wise double descent in test error.
rows.value: The authors state that after a marked decrease in accuracy in the first half, accuracy began increasing again in the second half, and identify the corresponding test-error pattern as epoch-wise double descent. No numeric values stated in the text.
rows.uncertainty: Five repetitions; mean accuracy and standard deviation were recorded, but numeric uncertainty for this result is not stated.
rows.note: The prose explicitly identifies the CIFAR-100 pattern but does not specify the method curve or noise panel. Figure 4 displays separate method and noise curves; this row records only the aggregate qualitative finding stated in the text, not a numeric average.
rows.check: The authors state the pattern (fall in the first half, rise in the second, ending above the early-stopping best), so 'observed' holds as their description. Two weaknesses should be flagged. First, the prose follows a sentence saying SIGUA_SL stopped or alleviated the decrease in Standard and Self-Teach, so the described curve may be the authors' own SIGUA_SL method, which applies gradient ascent on bad data, not plain training. Second, SET1 decays the learning rate linearly to 0 from epoch 80 to 200, a possible confound for the second rise. The noise panel is unidentified and no numbers are given.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B, Figure 4 discussion, lines 1619–1620 and 1972–1974; architecture in Appendix A, lines 1567–1569; repetitions in Section 4, lines 742–744.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, 9-layer CNN, SET1 noisy-label training (symmetric/pair noise), Adam with LR decayed to 0 after epoch 80; curve and method not identified
relationships.reason: The authors state test accuracy fell, then rose past the early-stopping best, and call it epoch-wise double descent (R1). The support is weak: qualitative only, possibly from the SIGUA_SL curve, and confounded by LR decay.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell and then exceeded its early-stopping best, although learning-rate decay complicates interpretation.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own epoch-wise double-descent observation in noisy-label learning experiments, a new application setting; double descent is an incidental observation rather than the method's central research question.

source_check.notes: The supplied year 2018 conflicts with the inspected version's ICML 2020 proceedings and October 2020 revision. The observation lacks numerical extrema or curve-specific attribution, and learning-rate decay overlaps the recovery.

statements.correction: SIGUA, arXiv:1809.11008v3, ICML 2020; CIFAR-100; 9 convolutional layers, 19 trainable layers; SET1: Standard, Self-Teach, SIGUA_SL; symmetry-20%, symmetry-50%, pair-45% panels; Adam; 200 epochs; linear learning-rate decay from epoch 80 to 200; five repetitions with mean and standard deviation. Appendix B reports accuracy recovery beyond the early-stopping best and identifies epoch-wise double descent in test error; specific method curve and noise panel unspecified.
statements.problem: The qualitative accuracy/error description matches R1, but none of the source-specific condition blocks identifies SIGUA. The cited row therefore lacks its own study attribution and conditions; no numerical effect size is asserted for this study.
